Liberalism is a political philosophy or worldview founded on ideas of liberty and equality.

The idea has been floating around for a long time but has never been fully practiced (and documented), not unlike laissez-faire economics (id est Capitalism), Communism, Meritocracies, et cetera. None have been fully realized by any society as far as I know.

Athens and Rome both eventually tried to take directions towards liberalism, but their ideas of freedom and equality were a lot different than the connotations we imply from those words today. The meanings of words change over time: faggot, for example.

Even the U.S.A. with its Declaration of Independence, and its Constitution, has never realized a completely free and equal state (liberalism). Originally, only people with property of/on US soil could vote. The reasoning for this was because they believed only people with a vested interest (id est financial interest) should have political interest in the State. The Colonies didn't like being taxed without representation in Parliament, and they hated Governmental (royal/Parliament) control of industries. So it was already the well-to-do who established the U.S.A. They were extremely liberal for their time. And to push away from a Monarch successfully, they even inspired others to do the same.

Yet, even some of the Founders knew that they were being hypocritical with their Declaration and simultaneous practice of slavery and limited suffrage. Fuckin' eh, 18-year-olds weren't allowed to vote in the U.S. until 1971 (it is the 26th Amendment to the Constitution). The Founders assumed every generation would fix their own problems with new establishments (Declarations/Constitutions/Bills of Rights) for a similar but more-progressed democratic government.

Here we are, we have given every 18+ year old the right to vote, they don't have to be male, white, 21+ years old, with property. The suffrage could only be better if teens and children could vote. That would be more equal, since they have a stake in what the fuck happens around them too.

You could think I'm sarcastic about this, but I believe children could make better decisions than our Congress. They could probably be easily manipulated, but I think enough voters are manipulated as is. What with the "Vote 'yes' on Proposition 8 which is an injunction on some other proposition from even being voted on" type of jiggery-pokery, voters don't know pure applesauce from a substitute. Children could make the more moral decision if they were informed as well as the average voter. We could teach children about political science at an earlier age, it's not like political science is hard (PoliSci slam).

The ideology of Liberalism definitely changes over time since the ideas of freedom and equality continue to change. Liberalism really is the ideology that has pushed the social boundaries forward for good. The side of progress triumphs in the long-run. And it has taken a longer run than it should. The reactionary side should be apprehensive about quick socioeconomic and political change, but they shouldn't be completely against it. They will never stop progress unless the nuke the world over, and even then I know humans would still progress, that would just be a set-back. There shouldn't even be a reactionary side that tries to prevent progress or even revert back (mostly social issues but some economical issues as well) to worn-out policies.
